title: Practice 3: Where to: в and на

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Представление в ___ (среда, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: The show's Wednesday.
exercises.why: **среда → среду** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -а. Declines like DLI's газета — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. газету). Ending -а → -у.  Declension: sg. среда · среды · среде · среду · средой · среде; pl. среды · сред · средам · среды · средами · средах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Таможенники поднялись на ___ (борт, acc. sg.) судна.
exercises.prompt: The customs officials boarded the ship.
exercises.why: **борт → борт** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. борт · борта · борту · борт · бортом · борте; pl. борта · бортов · бортам · борта · бортами · бортах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Закат окрасил небо в ___ (прекрасный цвет, acc. pl.).
exercises.prompt: The sunset painted the sky in beautiful colors.
exercises.why: **цвет → цвета** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural цвета. Declines like DLI's дом — every plural form has the same endings (A. pl. дома). Ending — (no ending) → -а.  **прекрасный → прекрасные** (acc. pl., agreeing with цвета). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. цвет · цвета · цвету · цвет · цветом · цвете; pl. цвета · цветов · цветам · цвета · цветами · цветах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Президент наложил вето на ___ (этот законопроект, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: The president vetoed that bill.
exercises.why: **законопроект → законопроект** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **этот → этот** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with законопроект). «этот» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (m. sg.): этот · этого · этому · этот (inan.) / этого (anim.) · этим · этом.  Declension: sg. законопроект · законопроекта · законопроекту · законопроект · законопроектом · законопроекте; pl. законопроекты · законопроектов · законопроектам · законопроекты · законопроектами · законопроектах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Роуз встала, чтобы положить розовую икру на ___ (свой ряд, acc. pl.) роз.
exercises.prompt: Rose rose to put rose roes on her rows of roses.
exercises.why: **ряд → ряды** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural ряды. Declines like DLI's стол — every plural form has the same endings (A. pl. столы). Ending — (no ending) → -ы.  **свой → свои** (acc. pl., agreeing with ряды). A possessive — declines like DLI's мой. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. ряд · ряда · ряду · ряд · рядом · ряде; pl. ряды · рядов · рядам · ряды · рядами · рядах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «Notice the similarity of the endings of the possessives to the form of «они».» мой · моё — моего — моему — моим — о моём; моя — моей — мою; мои — моих — моим — моими — о моих. — DLI, Lessons 47–48.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (последнее время, acc. sg.) все слишком подорожало.
exercises.prompt: These days, everything has got too expensive.
exercises.why: **время → время** (acc. sg.). Neuter, nominative singular in -мя. Declines like DLI's имя — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. имя). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **последний → последнее** (acc. sg. n., agreeing with время). Adjective type II, soft — declines like DLI's синий (every form has the same endings): A. синее. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. время · времени · времени · время · временем · времени; pl. времена · времён · временам · времена · временами · временах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
